name: The Ritz-Carlton Bacara
positioning: Spanish Colonial Revival beach resort on a bluff between the Pacific and the Santa Ynez Mountains, officially The Ritz-Carlton Bacara, Santa Barbara
best_for: Families who want nature programs and two-bedroom suites
Travelers who want a self-contained beach resort outside downtown Santa Barbara

facts.text: The resort sits on a bluff between the Pacific and the Santa Ynez Mountains in Santa Barbara.
The architecture is Spanish Colonial Revival, with stucco facades, arched doorways and hand-painted tilework.
The renovation was led by interior design firm Meyer Davis and added local art and Chumash motifs.
The Ritz-Carlton Suite is a two-bedroom suite of 2,000 sq ft with a separate living space, fireplace and kitchenette.
The Channel Island Suite is a two-bedroom suite of 3,700 sq ft that suits families or groups of up to eight.
Lulio serves Mediterranean-inspired fare highlighting local produce and sustainable seafood.
Marisella is an Italian restaurant serving handmade pastas and wood-grilled seafood.
The resort has four clay tennis courts next to the beach.
The resort welcomes dogs weighing 50 pounds or less in its one- and two-bedroom suites.

highlights.text: A multi-million-dollar renovation of the resort was completed in July 2025.
Families can join guided eco-hikes through the Gaviota Coast foothills and birding and butterfly bike-and-hike adventures.
'O' Bar & Terrace is named for the Chumash word for water and has an open-air loggia with ocean views.
Ambassadors of the Environment programs introduce guests to the Gaviota Coast, including kelp forest, birds, the intertidal zone and Chumash culture.

considerations.text: The resort is about 12 miles north of downtown Santa Barbara, and the city's shops and restaurants are roughly a 20-minute drive away.
The property is set on a hill, and an on-demand jitney cart service helps guests move around.
The resort has a resort fee, which comes with a set of included experiences.
